episode: Task: fix a path inside the director's own prompt file. The fix was a one-line `sed -i '' 's|(`docs/MEMORY-FORMAT.md`)|(the format is in `memory/README.md`)|'` on DIRECTOR.md. It exited 0 and the work moved on; the next arm ran with the old, broken path, because the text spanned a line break and the pattern matched nothing. Earlier the same day, a mutation test inserted a bug with `sed` using the wrong indentation: nothing changed, the suite stayed green, and only a second look showed the mutation had not been applied. Correction from review: after any scripted edit (sed, a regex replace, a search-and-replace script), check that it landed — grep for the new text, count the replacements, or read the diff — before relying on it or drawing a conclusion from what follows.

Task: run the conformance suite through the Python build of the CLI. The suite's runner copies each case into a fresh temporary directory and runs the given command there. The command passed was `--cli "crates/agentvcs-py/.venv/bin/python -m agentvcs"`, a path relative to the repository. Result: 0/117, every case failing. The implementation was fine: from the temporary directory the interpreter path did not exist; with the absolute path the same build passed 117/117. Correction from review: a command handed to a runner that executes it in another directory (temporary dirs, sandboxes, CI steps, gate suites) uses absolute paths, and an all-fail result is first read as a harness or path problem, not as the implementation failing.

Task: build a baseline arm that runs `claude -p` inside a sandbox directory and must load that directory's CLAUDE.md, the way a normal Claude Code session does. `claude -p --help` says `--bare` is a minimal mode that skips hooks, plugins, auto-memory, keychain reads and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery; `--restricted` removes the built-in tools that run code and ignores settings files, but keeps CLAUDE.md. A one-line probe — a CLAUDE.md holding a secret word, then asking for it — confirmed that `--restricted` loads CLAUDE.md. Lesson recorded: for an arm that must see project instructions use `--restricted`, not `--bare`, and prove the instructions are loaded with a probe before scoring anything.
